functions.name: initgraph
functions.description: Initializes the graphics system by loading a graphics driver from disk and putting the system into graphics mode. This must be called before any other graphics function.
functions.syntax: void far initgraph(int far *graphdriver, int far *graphmode, const char far *pathtodriver);

parameters.name: graphdriver
parameters.description: Pointer to an integer specifying the graphics driver to use. Pass DETECT (0) for auto-detection.

parameters.name: graphmode
parameters.description: Pointer to an integer specifying the initial graphics mode. Ignored when DETECT is used.

parameters.name: pathtodriver
parameters.description: Path to the directory containing the .BGI graphics driver files. Use empty string or NULL to search the current directory.

notes: Always call closegraph() when done to restore the original video mode.
Use graphresult() after initgraph() to check for errors.
When DETECT is passed, the system auto-detects the best available graphics driver and mode.

functions.name: closegraph
functions.description: Shuts down the graphics system, deallocates memory allocated by the graphics system, and restores the screen to the mode it was in before initgraph() was called.
notes: Always pair with initgraph() to avoid memory leaks.
After closegraph(), all graphics functions become invalid until initgraph() is called again.

functions.name: detectgraph
functions.description: Checks the hardware and determines the graphics driver and mode to use. Does not switch to graphics mode—use initgraph() for that.
functions.syntax: void far detectgraph(int far *graphdriver, int far *graphmode);

parameters.name: graphdriver
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the detected graphics driver constant (e.g., VGA, EGA, CGA).

parameters.name: graphmode
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the highest-resolution mode available for the detected driver.

notes: Returns grNotDetected (-2) in graphdriver if no graphics hardware is found.
Useful for querying hardware capabilities without entering graphics mode.

functions.name: restorecrtmode
functions.description: Temporarily restores the screen to the text mode that was active before initgraph() was called, without deallocating graphics memory.
notes: Use setgraphmode() to return to graphics mode after restorecrtmode().
Unlike closegraph(), this does NOT free graphics memory.

functions.name: graphdefaults
functions.description: Resets all graphics settings to their defaults: moves the current position to (0,0), resets viewport to the full screen, sets colors to white on black, and resets line style, fill style, and text settings.
notes: Does not clear the screen; call cleardevice() for that.
Useful to reset state between drawing operations.

functions.name: setgraphmode
functions.description: Selects a graphics mode different from the one set by initgraph(), clears the screen, and resets all graphics settings to their defaults.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: A valid graphics mode for the current driver (e.g., VGAHI, CGAC0). Use getmaxmode() to find the maximum valid mode.

notes: Clears the screen and resets drawing settings when called.
Can also be used to return to graphics mode after restorecrtmode().

functions.name: getgraphmode
functions.description: Returns the current graphics mode set by initgraph() or setgraphmode().
functions.returns: int — the current graphics mode number
notes: Returns the integer mode number, not the mode name.
Use getmodename() to get a string name for the mode.

functions.name: getmaxmode
functions.description: Returns the maximum valid mode number for the current graphics driver.
functions.returns: int — the maximum mode number for the loaded driver
notes: Useful when iterating through available modes.
Combine with getmoderange() for full mode range info.

functions.name: getmodename
functions.description: Returns a string containing the name of a specified graphics mode.
functions.returns: char * — pointer to a string describing the mode (e.g., "640 x 480 VGA")

parameters.name: mode_number
parameters.description: The graphics mode number whose name you want to retrieve.

notes: Returns a pointer to a statically allocated string; do not free it.
Useful for listing available modes to the user.

functions.name: getmoderange
functions.description: Returns the lowest and highest valid mode numbers for a specified graphics driver.
functions.syntax: void far getmoderange(int graphdriver, int far *lomode, int far *himode);

parameters.name: graphdriver
parameters.description: The graphics driver constant (e.g., VGA, EGA) for which to query the mode range.

parameters.name: lomode
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the lowest available mode number for the driver.

parameters.name: himode
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the highest available mode number for the driver.

notes: Can be called without initializing graphics.
Returns -1 in both lomode and himode if the driver is not valid.

functions.name: getdrivername
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a string containing the name of the current graphics driver.
functions.returns: char * — pointer to a string with the driver name (e.g., "VGA")
notes: Returns a pointer to a statically allocated string; do not free it.
Returns NULL if initgraph() has not been called.

functions.name: getmaxx
functions.description: Returns the maximum x-coordinate (screen width minus 1) for the current graphics mode.
functions.returns: int — the maximum x pixel coordinate
notes: In VGAHI mode (640x480), getmaxx() returns 639.
Use with getmaxy() to handle any screen resolution.

functions.name: getmaxy
functions.description: Returns the maximum y-coordinate (screen height minus 1) for the current graphics mode.
functions.returns: int — the maximum y pixel coordinate
notes: In VGAHI mode (640x480), getmaxy() returns 479.
Use with getmaxx() to build resolution-independent graphics.

functions.name: moveto
functions.description: Moves the current drawing position (CP) to the specified absolute coordinate (x, y) without drawing anything.
functions.syntax: void far moveto(int x, int y);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The absolute x-coordinate to move to.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The absolute y-coordinate to move to.

notes: Does not draw—only repositions the current position.
Coordinates are relative to the current viewport.

functions.name: moverel
functions.description: Moves the current drawing position (CP) by a relative offset (dx, dy) from its current location, without drawing.
functions.syntax: void far moverel(int dx, int dy);

parameters.name: dx
parameters.description: Horizontal offset from the current x position.

parameters.name: dy
parameters.description: Vertical offset from the current y position.

notes: Negative dx moves left; negative dy moves up.
Relative movement is from the current CP, not the origin.

functions.name: lineto
functions.description: Draws a line from the current drawing position (CP) to the specified absolute coordinate, then updates the CP to that endpoint.
functions.syntax: void far lineto(int x, int y);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Absolute x-coordinate of the endpoint.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Absolute y-coordinate of the endpoint.

notes: Updates the CP to the endpoint (x, y) after drawing.
Uses current color, line style, and thickness set by setlinestyle() and setcolor().

functions.name: linerel
functions.description: Draws a line from the current drawing position to a point offset by (dx, dy), then moves the CP to that new point.
functions.syntax: void far linerel(int dx, int dy);

parameters.name: dx
parameters.description: Horizontal offset from current x to the endpoint.

parameters.name: dy
parameters.description: Vertical offset from current y to the endpoint.

notes: Combines a move and a draw in relative coordinates.
Good for drawing shapes step-by-step from a starting point.

functions.name: line
functions.description: Draws a line between two specified absolute coordinates (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) without changing the current drawing position.
functions.syntax: void far line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2);

parameters.name: x1
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the starting point.

parameters.name: y1
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the starting point.

parameters.name: x2
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the ending point.

parameters.name: y2
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the ending point.

notes: Does NOT update the current drawing position.
Respects the current color, line style, and thickness.

functions.name: getx
functions.description: Returns the x-coordinate of the current drawing position (CP).
notes: Returns position relative to the current viewport.
Initially 0 after initgraph().

functions.name: gety
functions.description: Returns the y-coordinate of the current drawing position (CP).
notes: Returns position relative to the current viewport.
Initially 0 after initgraph().

functions.name: circle
functions.description: Draws a circle with a specified center and radius using the current drawing color.
functions.syntax: void far circle(int x, int y, int radius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the center.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Radius of the circle in pixels.

notes: The circle is adjusted for the aspect ratio of the screen; it may not be perfectly round at all resolutions.
Only draws the outline—use fillellipse() for a filled circle.
Line thickness is determined by setlinestyle(), but only NORM_WIDTH and THICK_WIDTH apply.

functions.name: arc
functions.description: Draws a circular arc from stangle to endangle with the specified center and radius, using the current drawing color.
functions.syntax: void far arc(int x, int y, int stangle, int endangle, int radius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the arc's center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the arc's center.

parameters.name: stangle
parameters.description: Starting angle in degrees (0 = 3 o'clock, increases counter-clockwise).

parameters.name: endangle
parameters.description: Ending angle in degrees.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Radius of the arc in pixels.

notes: Angles are in degrees, measured counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock (east).
To get the arc endpoints, call getarccoords() after drawing.
A full circle is drawn by passing stangle=0 and endangle=360.

functions.name: ellipse
functions.description: Draws an elliptical arc from stangle to endangle with specified x and y radii. Use stangle=0 and endangle=360 to draw a complete ellipse.
functions.syntax: void far ellipse(int x, int y, int stangle, int endangle, int xradius, int yradius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the ellipse center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the ellipse center.

parameters.name: stangle
parameters.description: Starting angle in degrees.

parameters.name: endangle
parameters.description: Ending angle in degrees.

parameters.name: xradius
parameters.description: Horizontal radius in pixels.

parameters.name: yradius
parameters.description: Vertical radius in pixels.

notes: Draws only the outline; use fillellipse() to fill.
When xradius == yradius and stangle=0, endangle=360, result is a circle.

functions.name: fillellipse
functions.description: Draws a filled ellipse with the specified center and x/y radii, using the current fill color and fill pattern.
functions.syntax: void far fillellipse(int x, int y, int xradius, int yradius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the ellipse center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the ellipse center.

parameters.name: xradius
parameters.description: Horizontal radius in pixels.

parameters.name: yradius
parameters.description: Vertical radius in pixels.

notes: Draws the border in the current drawing color and fills using setfillstyle().
When xradius == yradius, this draws a filled circle.

functions.name: rectangle
functions.description: Draws a rectangle outline with the specified corner coordinates using the current drawing color.
functions.syntax: void far rectangle(int left, int top, int right, int bottom);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the left edge.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the top edge.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the right edge.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the bottom edge.

notes: Draws only the outline; use bar() to draw a filled rectangle.
The CP is not changed by this function.

functions.name: bar
functions.description: Draws a filled (solid) rectangular bar using the current fill style and fill color. No border is drawn.
functions.syntax: void far bar(int left, int top, int right, int bottom);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the left edge.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the top edge.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the right edge.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the bottom edge.

notes: Does NOT draw a border. To draw a bordered filled rectangle, use rectangle() + floodfill() or bar3d() with depth=0.
Uses the fill style and color set by setfillstyle().

functions.name: bar3d
functions.description: Draws a three-dimensional filled rectangular bar with an optional top face, useful for creating bar charts with depth.
functions.syntax: void far bar3d(int left, int top, int right, int bottom, int depth, int topflag);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the left edge of the bar face.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the top edge of the bar face.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the right edge of the bar face.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the bottom edge of the bar face.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Depth of the 3D effect in pixels.

parameters.name: topflag
parameters.description: Non-zero to draw a 3D top; 0 to omit the top (useful when stacking bars).

notes: The border is drawn in the current drawing color; interior uses setfillstyle().
Set topflag=0 for the lower bars in a stacked bar chart.

functions.name: pieslice
functions.description: Draws and fills a pie slice (sector of a circle) with a specified center, start angle, end angle, and radius.
functions.syntax: void far pieslice(int x, int y, int stangle, int endangle, int radius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the pie's center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the pie's center.

parameters.name: stangle
parameters.description: Starting angle in degrees.

parameters.name: endangle
parameters.description: Ending angle in degrees.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Radius of the pie in pixels.

notes: The outline is drawn in the current color; the fill uses setfillstyle().
For elliptical pie slices, use sector().

functions.name: sector
functions.description: Draws and fills an elliptical sector (pie slice shape based on an ellipse) with specified center, angles, and x/y radii.
functions.syntax: void far sector(int x, int y, int stangle, int endangle, int xradius, int yradius);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the sector center.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the sector center.

parameters.name: stangle
parameters.description: Starting angle in degrees.

parameters.name: endangle
parameters.description: Ending angle in degrees.

parameters.name: xradius
parameters.description: Horizontal radius in pixels.

parameters.name: yradius
parameters.description: Vertical radius in pixels.

notes: Like pieslice() but for ellipses (xradius and yradius can differ).
The fill uses the current fill style set by setfillstyle().

functions.name: drawpoly
functions.description: Draws a polygon outline by connecting a series of points. To close the polygon, the last point should equal the first.
functions.syntax: void far drawpoly(int numpoints, const int far *polypoints);

parameters.name: numpoints
parameters.description: Number of points (vertices) in the polygon.

parameters.name: polypoints
parameters.description: Array of (x, y) coordinate pairs: {x0, y0, x1, y1, ...}.

notes: To close the polygon visually, the last point must equal the first point (requiring numpoints+1 entries).
Uses the current color and line style.

functions.name: fillpoly
functions.description: Draws and fills a polygon using the current fill style and color. The polygon is automatically closed.
functions.syntax: void far fillpoly(int numpoints, const int far *polypoints);

parameters.name: numpoints
parameters.description: Number of vertices in the polygon.

parameters.name: polypoints
parameters.description: Array of (x, y) coordinate pairs: {x0, y0, x1, y1, ...}.

notes: Automatically closes the polygon (no need to repeat the first point).
The outline is drawn in the current drawing color; fill uses setfillstyle().

functions.name: floodfill
functions.description: Flood-fills an enclosed area starting from the point (x, y). The fill stops at pixels matching the specified border color.
functions.syntax: void far floodfill(int x, int y, int border);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the seed point (must be inside the boundary).

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the seed point.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: Color of the boundary to stop filling at.

notes: The seed point (x, y) must be inside the enclosed region.
If the boundary is not fully closed, fill will leak outside.
Uses the current fill style set by setfillstyle().

functions.name: setcolor
functions.description: Sets the current drawing (foreground) color used for lines, borders, text, and outlines.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Color value from the COLORS enum (e.g., RED, BLUE) or a palette index 0–getmaxcolor().

notes: Available colors depend on the current graphics mode and driver.
Use getmaxcolor() to find the maximum valid color index.

functions.name: getcolor
functions.description: Returns the current drawing (foreground) color.
functions.returns: int — the current foreground color index
notes: Default color is WHITE (15) after initgraph().
Returned value is a palette index, not an RGB value.

functions.name: setbkcolor
functions.description: Sets the background color of the graphics screen. The entire background is filled with this color.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Background color from the COLORS enum or a palette index.

notes: The background change takes effect immediately for new drawing but does not repaint existing pixels.
Default background is BLACK.

functions.name: getbkcolor
functions.description: Returns the current background color.
functions.returns: int — the current background color index
notes: Default is BLACK (0) after initgraph().

functions.name: getmaxcolor
functions.description: Returns the maximum valid color index for the current graphics mode.
functions.returns: int — the highest valid color index
notes: Returns 15 for 16-color VGA/EGA modes.
Returns 255 for 256-color modes (IBM8514).
Useful to write mode-independent color code.

functions.name: setpalette
functions.description: Changes one entry in the color palette, remapping a palette index to a new color value.
functions.syntax: void far setpalette(int colornum, int color);

parameters.name: colornum
parameters.description: The palette entry index to change (0 to getmaxcolor()).

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The new color value (from EGA_COLORS or similar driver-specific constants).

notes: EGA/VGA use EGA_COLORS constants; CGA uses CGA_COLORS.
Changing palette index 0 changes the background color.
Changes affect all pixels already drawn with that color index.

functions.name: setallpalette
functions.description: Sets all palette entries at once using a palettetype structure.
functions.syntax: void far setallpalette(const struct palettetype far *palette);

parameters.name: palette
parameters.description: Pointer to a palettetype structure containing the new palette values for all colors.

notes: The palettetype structure has a size field and a colors array.
Use getpalette() first to get the current palette before modifying.

functions.name: getpalette
functions.description: Retrieves the current palette settings into a palettetype structure.

parameters.name: palette
parameters.description: Pointer to a palettetype structure to be filled with current palette data.

notes: The palettetype structure has a size field (number of colors) and a colors array (signed char[16]).
Used to save palette before modifications.

functions.name: getdefaultpalette
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the default palette for the current graphics driver.
functions.returns: struct palettetype far * — pointer to the default palette
notes: Returns a pointer to a static structure; do not free it.
Useful for restoring the default palette after modifications.

functions.name: getpalettesize
functions.description: Returns the number of entries in the color palette for the current driver and mode.
notes: Returns 16 for EGA/VGA 16-color modes, 256 for IBM8514.
Same as MAXCOLORS+1 in most cases.

functions.name: setrgbpalette
functions.description: Sets a palette entry to a specific RGB color. Only valid for IBM8514 and VGA drivers that support direct RGB palette setting.
functions.syntax: void far setrgbpalette(int colornum, int red, int green, int blue);

parameters.name: colornum
parameters.description: The palette index to set.

parameters.name: red
parameters.description: Red intensity (0–63 for EGA/VGA DAC).

parameters.name: green
parameters.description: Green intensity (0–63).

parameters.name: blue
parameters.description: Blue intensity (0–63).

requirements: initgraph() with IBM8514 or compatible driver
notes: Values range from 0 to 63 (6-bit DAC), not 0–255.
Only works on drivers that support direct RGB palette programming.

functions.name: setaspectratio
functions.description: Overrides the default aspect ratio used when drawing circles and arcs, allowing correction for non-square pixels.
functions.syntax: void far setaspectratio(int xasp, int yasp);

parameters.name: xasp
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect ratio value.

parameters.name: yasp
parameters.description: Vertical aspect ratio value.

notes: The ratio xasp/yasp determines the scaling. A higher yasp relative to xasp makes circles appear wider.
Use getaspectratio() to read the current values before changing.

functions.name: getaspectratio
functions.description: Returns the current aspect ratio used by the graphics system for circular shapes.
functions.syntax: void far getaspectratio(int far *xasp, int far *yasp);

parameters.name: xasp
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the horizontal aspect ratio.

parameters.name: yasp
parameters.description: Pointer filled with the vertical aspect ratio.

notes: Used internally by circle() to produce visually round shapes.
Typically xasp == 10000 and yasp varies by mode.

functions.name: setlinestyle
functions.description: Sets the style (solid, dashed, dotted, etc.), pattern, and thickness for lines drawn by line(), lineto(), etc.
functions.syntax: void far setlinestyle(int linestyle, unsigned upattern, int thickness);

parameters.name: linestyle
parameters.description: Line style constant: SOLID_LINE, DOTTED_LINE, CENTER_LINE, DASHED_LINE, or USERBIT_LINE.

parameters.name: upattern
parameters.description: 16-bit custom pattern used only when linestyle is USERBIT_LINE. Ignored for other styles.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Line thickness: NORM_WIDTH (1) or THICK_WIDTH (3).

notes: USERBIT_LINE uses the upattern value as a 16-bit bitmask for the line pattern.
Thickness only supports NORM_WIDTH (1 pixel) and THICK_WIDTH (3 pixels).

functions.name: getlinesettings
functions.description: Retrieves the current line style, pattern, and thickness settings into a linesettingstype structure.

parameters.name: lineinfo
parameters.description: Pointer to a linesettingstype structure to be filled with current line settings.

notes: The linesettingstype struct has linestyle, upattern, and thickness fields.
Useful for saving and restoring line settings.

functions.name: setfillstyle
functions.description: Sets the fill pattern and fill color used by filled drawing functions like bar(), fillpoly(), and floodfill().
functions.syntax: void far setfillstyle(int pattern, int color);

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Fill pattern from fill_patterns enum: SOLID_FILL, HATCH_FILL, SLASH_FILL, EMPTY_FILL, etc.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Fill color index (from COLORS enum or palette index).

notes: EMPTY_FILL fills with the current background color.
USER_FILL requires setfillpattern() to define the custom 8x8 pattern.
SOLID_FILL is the most commonly used pattern.

functions.name: getfillsettings
functions.description: Retrieves the current fill pattern and color settings into a fillsettingstype structure.

parameters.name: fillinfo
parameters.description: Pointer to a fillsettingstype structure to fill with current settings.

notes: The fillsettingstype struct has pattern and color fields.

functions.name: setfillpattern
functions.description: Selects a user-defined 8x8 fill pattern (8 bytes, one per row) and a fill color for USER_FILL mode.
functions.syntax: void far setfillpattern(const char far *upattern, int color);

parameters.name: upattern
parameters.description: Pointer to an 8-byte array defining the 8x8 pixel fill pattern (each bit = 1 pixel).

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Fill color to use with this pattern.

notes: Each byte represents one horizontal row of 8 pixels. Bit 1 = color pixel, bit 0 = background pixel.
Must also call setfillstyle(USER_FILL, color) or ensure USER_FILL is active—setfillpattern sets both.

functions.name: getfillpattern
functions.description: Copies the current user-defined fill pattern into the provided 8-byte array.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Pointer to an 8-byte array to receive the current fill pattern.

notes: Returns the user-defined pattern; does not return built-in patterns like HATCH_FILL.

functions.name: cleardevice
functions.description: Clears the entire graphics screen by filling it with the current background color and moves the current position to (0,0).
notes: Resets the current position to (0, 0).
Uses the current background color to clear.

functions.name: clearviewport
functions.description: Clears only the current viewport (not the entire screen) by filling it with the background color, and moves the CP to the viewport's top-left corner.
notes: Only affects the current viewport area.
Coordinate (0,0) in the viewport maps to its top-left corner.

functions.name: setviewport
functions.description: Defines a rectangular viewport (clipping region). After this call, all drawing is relative to the viewport's top-left corner.
functions.syntax: void far setviewport(int left, int top, int right, int bottom, int clip);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Absolute x of the viewport's left edge.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Absolute y of the viewport's top edge.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Absolute x of the viewport's right edge.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Absolute y of the viewport's bottom edge.

parameters.name: clip
parameters.description: Non-zero to enable clipping (drawing outside viewport is hidden); 0 to disable clipping.

notes: After setviewport(), coordinate (0,0) refers to (left, top) on screen.
Call setviewport(0, 0, getmaxx(), getmaxy(), 1) to reset to full screen.

functions.name: getviewsettings
functions.description: Retrieves the current viewport coordinates and clipping flag into a viewporttype structure.

parameters.name: viewport
parameters.description: Pointer to a viewporttype structure to fill with current viewport settings.

notes: The viewporttype struct has: left, top, right, bottom (all int) and clip (int).
Coordinates are absolute screen coordinates, not relative.

functions.name: setactivepage
functions.description: Sets the active graphics page for drawing. Drawing goes to the specified page, which may or may not be the currently visible page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to draw on (0-based; available pages depend on the video mode).

requirements: initgraph() with a driver/mode supporting multiple pages (e.g., EGA, VGA)
notes: EGA 640x350 supports 2 pages; CGA supports 1 page.
Combine with setvisualpage() for flicker-free double-buffering animation.

functions.name: setvisualpage
functions.description: Sets the page number that is currently displayed on screen, enabling page-flipping for smooth animation.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to display (0-based).

notes: Switching the visual page is instantaneous (hardware-level operation).
Eliminates tearing artifacts compared to drawing directly to the visible page.

functions.name: setwritemode
functions.description: Sets the logical write mode for line drawing. The default is COPY_PUT; XOR_PUT allows lines to be erased by redrawing them.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Write mode: COPY_PUT (overwrite) or XOR_PUT (exclusive OR, for rubber-banding effects).

notes: XOR_PUT is useful for interactive rubber-band lines and animation without clearing the background.
Only affects functions that draw lines (line, lineto, linerel, rectangle, drawpoly).

functions.name: outtext
functions.description: Displays a string at the current drawing position (CP) using the current font, text direction, size, and color.

parameters.name: textstring
parameters.description: The null-terminated string to display.

notes: After drawing, the CP moves to the end of the string.
Use outtextxy() to specify an exact position without moving the CP first.

functions.name: outtextxy
functions.description: Displays a string at a specified (x, y) position using the current font settings.
functions.syntax: void far outtextxy(int x, int y, const char far *textstring);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the text's left (or justified) position.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the text's top (or justified) position.

parameters.name: textstring
parameters.description: Null-terminated string to display.

notes: Does not change the current position.
Justification is affected by settextjustify().

functions.name: settextstyle
functions.description: Sets the font, direction (horizontal or vertical), and character size for subsequent text output.
functions.syntax: void far settextstyle(int font, int direction, int charsize);

parameters.name: font
parameters.description: Font constant from font_names enum: DEFAULT_FONT, TRIPLEX_FONT, SMALL_FONT, SANS_SERIF_FONT, GOTHIC_FONT, etc.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: HORIZ_DIR (0) for left-to-right, VERT_DIR (1) for bottom-to-top.

parameters.name: charsize
parameters.description: Character size multiplier (1–10). Use 0 (USER_CHAR_SIZE) with setusercharsize() for custom scaling.

requirements: Corresponding .CHR font files in the BGI path (for non-default fonts)
notes: DEFAULT_FONT is a built-in 8x8 bitmap font; others are stroked fonts requiring .CHR files.
Stroked fonts scale smoothly at any size; bitmap font only doubles at size 2+.

functions.name: settextjustify
functions.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical alignment of text drawn by outtext() and outtextxy() relative to the given position.
functions.syntax: void far settextjustify(int horiz, int vert);

parameters.name: horiz
parameters.description: Horizontal justification: LEFT_TEXT (0), CENTER_TEXT (1), or RIGHT_TEXT (2).

parameters.name: vert
parameters.description: Vertical justification: BOTTOM_TEXT (0), CENTER_TEXT (1), or TOP_TEXT (2).

notes: Default is LEFT_TEXT, TOP_TEXT.
Justification applies to both outtext() and outtextxy().

functions.name: setusercharsize
functions.description: Defines a custom character size for stroked fonts when charsize is set to USER_CHAR_SIZE (0) in settextstyle().
functions.syntax: void far setusercharsize(int multx, int divx, int multy, int divy);

parameters.name: multx
parameters.description: Horizontal size multiplier.

parameters.name: divx
parameters.description: Horizontal size divisor. Character width = default_width * multx / divx.

parameters.name: multy
parameters.description: Vertical size multiplier.

parameters.name: divy
parameters.description: Vertical size divisor. Character height = default_height * multy / divy.

notes: Only works with stroked fonts (not the default bitmap font).
Must call settextstyle() with charsize=USER_CHAR_SIZE (0) first.

functions.name: gettextsettings
functions.description: Retrieves the current text font, direction, size, and justification settings into a textsettingstype structure.

parameters.name: texttypeinfo
parameters.description: Pointer to a textsettingstype structure to fill with current text settings.

notes: The textsettingstype struct has: font, direction, charsize, horiz, and vert fields.

functions.name: textheight
functions.description: Returns the height of a string in pixels based on the current font and character size.
functions.returns: int — height of the text in pixels

parameters.name: textstring
parameters.description: The string to measure (content doesn't affect height for standard fonts).

notes: For DEFAULT_FONT, height is always the same regardless of the string content.
Useful for centering or spacing text precisely.

functions.name: textwidth
functions.description: Returns the width in pixels of the specified string with the current font and character size.
functions.returns: int — width of the text string in pixels

parameters.name: textstring
parameters.description: The string to measure.

notes: Width varies by the actual characters in the string for stroked fonts.
Use with textheight() to perfectly center text on screen.

functions.name: putpixel
functions.description: Sets the color of a single pixel at the specified (x, y) coordinate.
functions.syntax: void far putpixel(int x, int y, int color);

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the pixel.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the pixel.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Color index to set.

notes: Color 0 effectively erases the pixel (sets to background).
Coordinates outside the current viewport are ignored if clipping is on.

functions.name: getpixel
functions.description: Returns the color of the pixel at the specified (x, y) coordinate.
functions.syntax: unsigned far getpixel(int x, int y);
functions.returns: unsigned — the color index of the pixel at (x, y)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the pixel to read.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the pixel to read.

notes: Returns the palette index, not an RGB value.
Reading outside the screen may return undefined values.

functions.name: getimage
functions.description: Saves a rectangular region of the screen into a memory buffer for later restoration with putimage().
functions.syntax: void far getimage(int left, int top, int right, int bottom, void far *bitmap);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Left x-coordinate of the region.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Top y-coordinate of the region.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Right x-coordinate of the region.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Bottom y-coordinate of the region.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.description: Pointer to a memory buffer large enough to store the image. Use imagesize() to determine the required buffer size.

notes: Always call imagesize() first to allocate the correct buffer size.
The buffer includes a header with width and height information.

functions.name: putimage
functions.description: Draws a bitmap image (previously saved by getimage()) onto the screen at the specified position, using a bitwise operation.
functions.syntax: void far putimage(int left, int top, const void far *bitmap, int op);

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the top-left corner where the image will be drawn.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the top-left corner where the image will be drawn.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.description: Pointer to the image buffer previously filled by getimage().

parameters.name: op
parameters.description: Bitwise operation: COPY_PUT (overwrite), XOR_PUT, OR_PUT, AND_PUT, or NOT_PUT.

notes: XOR_PUT is useful for animation—drawing twice restores the background.
OR_PUT and AND_PUT can create masking effects.

functions.name: imagesize
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to store a bitmap of the specified rectangular region, for use with getimage().
functions.syntax: unsigned far imagesize(int left, int top, int right, int bottom);
functions.returns: unsigned — bytes needed to store the region

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Left x-coordinate of the region.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Top y-coordinate.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Right x-coordinate.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.description: Bottom y-coordinate.

notes: If the region is too large for a single unsigned int to represent, returns 0xFFFF (-1).
Always call this before malloc-ing a buffer for getimage().

functions.name: getarccoords
functions.description: Retrieves the start and end pixel coordinates of the most recently drawn arc or pieslice.

parameters.name: arccoords
parameters.description: Pointer to an arccoordstype structure to fill with arc endpoint data.

requirements: arc() or pieslice() called before getarccoords()
notes: The arccoordstype struct has: x, y (center), xstart, ystart (start point), xend, yend (end point).
Useful for connecting lines from arc endpoints.

functions.name: installuserdriver
functions.description: Installs a user-supplied graphics driver into the BGI device driver table, allowing custom hardware support.
functions.syntax: int far installuserdriver(const char far *name, int huge (*detect)(void));
functions.returns: int — the driver number assigned, or a negative error code

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The filename (without extension) of the custom .BGI driver.

parameters.name: detect
parameters.description: Pointer to an autodetect function that returns the recommended mode, or NULL.

notes: Must be called before initgraph().
The detect function should return the graphics mode number if the hardware is found, or -1 if not.

functions.name: installuserfont
functions.description: Loads and installs a stroked font (.CHR file) that is not part of the standard BGI font set.
functions.returns: int — font number assigned, or a negative error code

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Path and filename (without .CHR extension) of the custom font file.

notes: Must be called before initgraph().
Returns a font number that can be passed to settextstyle().

functions.name: registerbgidriver
functions.description: Registers a graphics driver that has been linked directly into the executable (as an object file), so it does not need to be loaded from disk.
functions.returns: int — 0 on success, or a negative error code

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Pointer to the driver function (e.g., EGAVGA_driver, CGA_driver) linked into the program.

requirements: Link the corresponding driver object (e.g., EGAVGA.OBJ) into your project
notes: Allows distribution of standalone .EXE files without .BGI driver files.
Use registerfarbgidriver() for drivers in far memory.

functions.name: registerfarbgidriver
functions.description: Registers a graphics driver located in far memory (e.g., the _far arrays like EGAVGA_driver_far).
functions.returns: int — 0 on success, or a negative error code

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Far pointer to the driver data (e.g., EGAVGA_driver_far).

requirements: Link the appropriate far driver object file
notes: Use the _far[] array variants (e.g., EGAVGA_driver_far[]) when working with far memory models.
Needed for large/huge memory model programs.

functions.name: registerbgifont
functions.description: Registers a BGI font that has been linked into the executable so it can be used without a .CHR file on disk.
functions.returns: int — 0 on success, or a negative error code

parameters.name: font
parameters.description: Pointer to the font function (e.g., triplex_font, gothic_font) linked into the program.

requirements: Link corresponding font object file (e.g., TRIP.OBJ)
notes: Allows creating .EXE files without needing separate .CHR font files.
Use registerfarbgifont() for far memory model programs.

functions.name: registerfarbgifont
functions.description: Registers a BGI font stored in far memory (using the _far[] array variants).
functions.returns: int — 0 on success, or a negative error code

parameters.name: font
parameters.description: Far pointer to the font data array (e.g., triplex_font_far).

requirements: Link corresponding far font object file
notes: Use with large/huge memory model Turbo C programs.
Equivalent to registerbgifont() but for far memory pointers.

functions.name: _graphgetmem
functions.description: Allocates memory for the graphics system. This is an internal function used by the BGI; it can be replaced to use a custom memory allocator.
functions.returns: void far * — pointer to allocated memory, or NULL on failure

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of bytes to allocate.

notes: Not typically called directly by user programs.
Can be replaced to use a custom far heap or track graphics memory usage.

functions.name: _graphfreemem
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by _graphgetmem(). This is an internal BGI function that can be replaced for custom memory management.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: Pointer to the memory block to free.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the memory block in bytes.

notes: Not typically called by user programs.
Override as a pair with _graphgetmem() for custom memory management.

functions.name: setgraphbufsize
functions.description: Sets the size of the internal buffer used by the graphics system for scan-line fill operations. Call before initgraph().

parameters.name: bufsize
parameters.description: The new buffer size in bytes. Default is 4096.

notes: Increase the buffer size if floodfill() fails on large or complex areas.
Larger buffer uses more memory but allows filling larger regions.

functions.name: graphresult
functions.description: Returns the error code for the last unsuccessful graphics operation, then resets the internal error code to grOk (0).
functions.returns: int — error code from the graphics_errors enum (0 = grOk, negative = error)
notes: Always call immediately after initgraph() to catch initialization errors.
Once read, the error code is cleared to grOk—save the value if you need it multiple times.
Error codes range from 0 (grOk) to -18 (grInvalidVersion).

functions.name: grapherrormsg
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the specified graphics error code.
functions.returns: char * — pointer to an error message string

parameters.name: errorcode
parameters.description: An error code from the graphics_errors enum (e.g., grNoInitGraph, grFileNotFound).

notes: Returns a pointer to a static string; do not free it.
Can be called without initializing graphics—useful for early error reporting.

functions.name: grOk
functions.description: No error. The graphics operation completed successfully.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grOk) { /* success */ }

notes: Returned by graphresult() when no error has occurred.

functions.name: grNoInitGraph
functions.description: Error code -1: A graphics function was called before initgraph() was called.

example.code: circle(100,100,50); /* Without initgraph → graphresult() == grNoInitGraph */

notes: Always call initgraph() before any drawing function.

functions.name: grNotDetected
functions.description: Error code -2: No graphics hardware was detected by the auto-detection routine.

example.code:
/* Check after initgraph with DETECT */
if (graphresult() == grNotDetected) { /* No graphics card */ }

notes: Occurs when DETECT is used but no supported graphics card is found.

functions.name: grFileNotFound
functions.description: Error code -3: The specified BGI driver or font file could not be found on disk.
notes: Check the BGI path passed to initgraph(); ensure .BGI files are present.

functions.name: grInvalidDriver
functions.description: Error code -4: The found BGI file is not a valid graphics driver.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grInvalidDriver) { /* Corrupt or wrong .BGI */ }

notes: Ensure the .BGI file is not corrupted and matches the Borland format.

functions.name: grNoLoadMem
functions.description: Error code -5: Not enough memory to load the graphics driver.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grNoLoadMem) { /* Insufficient RAM for driver */ }

notes: Free memory before calling initgraph() if this error occurs.

functions.name: grNoScanMem
functions.description: Error code -6: Not enough memory to perform a scan-fill operation (e.g., floodfill).

example.code:
floodfill(100, 100, WHITE);
if (graphresult() == grNoScanMem) { /* Increase setgraphbufsize */ }

notes: Increase the scan buffer with setgraphbufsize() before initgraph() to fix this.

functions.name: grNoFloodMem
functions.description: Error code -7: Not enough memory to perform a flood-fill operation.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grNoFloodMem) { /* Not enough memory to flood fill */ }

notes: Similar to grNoScanMem; increase the graphics buffer or free memory.

functions.name: grFontNotFound
functions.description: Error code -8: The requested .CHR font file could not be found.

example.code:
settextstyle(TRIPLEX_FONT, HORIZ_DIR, 3);
if (graphresult() == grFontNotFound) { /* TRIP.CHR not found */ }

notes: Ensure the .CHR font files are in the BGI directory or link fonts with registerbgifont().

functions.name: grNoFontMem
functions.description: Error code -9: Not enough memory to load the requested font.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grNoFontMem) { /* Not enough memory for font */ }

notes: Free memory or use a smaller/simpler font.

functions.name: grInvalidMode
functions.description: Error code -10: An invalid graphics mode was specified for the current driver.

example.code:
setgraphmode(99); /* Invalid mode */
if (graphresult() == grInvalidMode) { /* Bad mode number */ }

notes: Use getmaxmode() to verify valid modes before calling setgraphmode().

functions.name: grError
functions.description: Error code -11: Generic/unspecified graphics error.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grError) { /* Generic graphics error */ }

notes: A catch-all error code for errors that don't fit a specific category.

functions.name: grIOerror
functions.description: Error code -12: I/O error while reading a driver or font file from disk.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grIOerror) { /* Disk I/O error */ }

notes: Check disk integrity and ensure sufficient disk space.

functions.name: grInvalidFont
functions.description: Error code -13: The .CHR font file found is not a valid BGI font.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grInvalidFont) { /* Corrupt or wrong CHR file */ }

notes: Ensure font files are genuine Borland .CHR files and are not corrupted.

functions.name: grInvalidFontNum
functions.description: Error code -14: An invalid font number was passed to settextstyle().

example.code:
settextstyle(99, HORIZ_DIR, 2); /* Invalid font number */
if (graphresult() == grInvalidFontNum) { /* Bad font # */ }

notes: Font numbers above BOLD_FONT (10) are only valid if additional fonts were installed.

functions.name: grInvalidVersion
functions.description: Error code -18: The BGI driver or font file is an incompatible version.

example.code: if (graphresult() == grInvalidVersion) { /* Wrong BGI/CHR version */ }

notes: Ensure all .BGI and .CHR files match the version of Turbo C being used.
